clue.text: Knight among more cult characters turned out a sad creature

indicators.note: among says the knight's letters sit inside the other group
turned out signals the letters of more cult are rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight mixing with members of a cult turns out to be a miserable being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like part of the surface's sad tale but is the anagram signal; 'among' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Carroll's Wonderland the Mock Turtle is a melancholy beast forever sobbing over his past.

clue.text: Nameless horrible creature catching Boots, initially a member of the gang

indicators.note: catching says the beast holds a letter inside it
Nameless says the abbreviation for name is removed

parts.note: a monster is a horrible creature

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An unnamed beast seizes some footwear, being one of a criminal band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' removes N (name) from MONSTER to give MOSTER; 'catching' puts B, from 'Boots, initially', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobster is a gangster, one of an organised criminal crew.

clue.text: Support for a growing girl's need

definitions.text: Support for a growing girl's need

parts.words: Support for a growing girl's need
parts.note: sounds like underwear for a teenager, but means a holder for the cake Alice eats to grow

explanation.surface: A garment a young girl needs as she develops.
explanation.walkthrough: In Wonderland Alice eats a cake marked EAT ME and grows enormously.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand on which a cake is displayed holds what Alice needs to grow.

clue.text: Girl hushed Kitty, endlessly shaken? It's sweet

indicators.note: shaken says these letters are tossed into a new order
endlessly drops the final letter of Kitty

explanation.surface: A girl quietens Alice's cat, and perhaps rattles it, all very sweetly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts KITTY to KITT; 'shaken' rearranges GIRL, HUSHED and KITT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gel-like confection dusted in sugar, it is a well-known sweet.

clue.text: Shaking violently following wild creature — no end of quest

indicators.note: no says the letter after it is dropped

parts.note: tracking is following an animal in the wild

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of quest

explanation.surface: Trembling while trailing a beast, without any result from the search.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' plus 'end of quest' removes T from TRACKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Racking means wrenching or convulsing, as a racking cough shakes the body.

clue.text: Joined with king going in a file

indicators.note: going says the king departs from the phrase

parts.note: linked up means joined
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Teaming up with a monarch as he enters a dossier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' takes K out of LINKED UP.
explanation.definitionFit: People lined up stand one behind another in a queue or row.

clue.text: Piece of card

definitions.meaning: a chessman, the most important on the board
a court card ranking above the queen

explanation.definitionFit: The monarch is both the key chessman and the picture card above the queen.

clue.text: I run with a queen, one inhabitant of divided land?

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
Q is the chess abbreviation for queen
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Alice runs beside a queen, as a pawn on the chessboard land.
explanation.walkthrough: The land between the Tigris and Euphrates is divided by rivers, as the Looking-glass land is divided into squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq, old Mesopotamia, is literally the land between two rivers.

clue.text: County Nell and Edward reached at last

parts.note: Nell Gwyn was Charles II's actress mistress
Ed is short for Edward

indicators.note: at last picks the closing letter of reached

explanation.surface: A Welsh shire that Nell and Edward finally arrived in.
explanation.definitionFit: Gwynedd is a county of north-west Wales.

clue.text: Powerlessly falling in earth, I have a peculiar resistance

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the words before it are set out strangely

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone drops limply to the ground with an odd reluctance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' rearranges IN EARTH I HAVE A into HEAVIERTHANAI, then R ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything denser than the atmosphere drops unless driven by an engine or lift.

clue.text: He came to a dreadful end, in agony

definitions.text: He came to a dreadful end, in agony

parts.words: He came to a dreadful end, in agony
parts.note: Carroll's Hunting of the Snark is subtitled An Agony in Eight Fits; one of its hunters softly and suddenly vanishes away on meeting a Boojum

explanation.surface: A man suffered terribly and died a horrible death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in agony' looks like pain but points to the poem's subtitle, An Agony in Eight Fits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baker is the Snark hunter who meets the Boojum and vanishes at the poem's close.

clue.text: Any recent novel writer has one today

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of any recent are set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Some recent novel's author celebrates an anniversary today.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared on 14 January 1998, a hundred years to the day after Lewis Carroll died, hence the Alice theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundredth anniversary is what Lewis Carroll marked on the day of publication.

clue.text: Gave evidence in trial, one launched after Queen's loss

parts.note: a test is a trial
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: loss says the queen's letter goes missing from the word before it

parts.note: a missile fired is launched
R, for Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: In a court case a witness spoke after a rocket was fired once the Queen had died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loss' removes R (Regina) from FIRED, leaving FIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to give sworn evidence as a witness.

clue.text: Bill lacking in power of speech

indicators.note: lacking says the following word is missing from the bill

parts.note: an invoice is a bill
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parliamentary bill falls short in the art of public speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes IN off the front of INVOICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Voice is the faculty of uttering sounds and words.

clue.text: One turning into a pig on the way?

definitions.text: One turning into a pig on the way?

parts.words: One turning into a pig on the way?
parts.note: recalls the baby in Wonderland that turns into a piglet, but read as a driver who becomes a swine on the road

explanation.surface: Someone metamorphoses into a pig during a journey, as the Duchess's baby did.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfish, aggressive driver is called a swine of the highway.

clue.text: Argued in court quietly, like old-fashioned type

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quietly
metal type was spaced with strips of lead, so set type was leaded

explanation.surface: A barrister spoke softly, in the manner of an old printing press.
explanation.walkthrough: Hand-set printing used lead strips between lines; such lines were 'leaded'.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel pleads a case when presenting arguments before a judge.

clue.text: A really good time to produce TV broadcast with 25

parts.note: to do a play is to produce it

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread about anew

parts.note: 25-across is Carroll's heroine

explanation.surface: Making a television programme of Carroll's tale would be a lot of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges TV with the answer to 25 across, giving LCEVITA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase means the sweet life, one of luxury and pleasure.

clue.text: In sorry state, is lad in mess? Off with their heads!

indicators.note: the Queen of Hearts' cry here beheads each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A boy in a muddle is in a bad way, and the Queen of Hearts orders executions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off with their heads!' drops the first letters of IS, LAD, IN and MESS, leaving S, AD, N and ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadness is sorrow, the condition of someone sorry or downcast.

clue.text: Hit suddenly distributes cards, going up about two metres

indicators.note: about says the reversed word goes round the metres
going up in a down clue means read from the bottom

parts.note: a card player deals
M is the abbreviation for metre, so two give MM

explanation.surface: A dealer slaps down cards and climbs a couple of metres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' reverses in a down clue, where the entry reads from the top; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To slam is to strike or shut with sudden force.

clue.text: Noted female, thoroughly wet, had a race — with duck

parts.note: a sop is something soaked through
ran means took part in a race
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A famous woman, soaked through, ran a race and scored nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Wonderland the soaked creatures, the Duck among them, run the Caucus-race to get dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a woman who sings the high notes, a 'noted' female.

clue.text: Thanks to Through the Looking-glass, initially, Queen's seen as gossip

parts.note: ta is an informal British thank you

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of the three title words

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Thanks to Carroll's sequel, the Queen gets a reputation as a busybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes T, T and L from Through the Looking-glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattler is a chatterer who spreads idle talk about others.

clue.text: Laughed to observe next tea being announced

indicators.note: next puts the sound-alike beside the word for observe
being announced says the drink is spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: the drink at the Mad Hatter's party
to heed is to take notice of

explanation.surface: A giggle at seeing the next cup of tea being served at the Hatter's party.
explanation.definitionFit: A tee-hee is a titter, so to tee-hee is to giggle.

clue.text: Take steps again to enjoy book afresh — about time

indicators.note: about says the word for reading again goes round time

parts.note: to reread is to read a book again

explanation.surface: Revisiting a favourite book once more after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts T inside REREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To retread a path is to walk over it once more.

clue.text: Some opera's said to be very musical

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark about opera being highly melodic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes the run ASSAI from operA'S SAId.
explanation.definitionFit: In Italian tempo markings the word means very, as in allegro assai, so it is 'very' in musical terms.

clue.text: Queen gave off about such a small amount of evidence?

definitions.text: such a small amount of evidence?

indicators.note: about says the word for gave off goes round the queen

parts.note: shed means gave off, as a tree sheds leaves
R, for Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen of Hearts emitted barely a trace of proof at the trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny scrap, as in 'not a shred of evidence', is the least possible amount.

clue.text: Quiet tear about farewell — not unusual

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

indicators.note: about says the tear goes round the farewell

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
vale is Latin for farewell

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken tearful goodbye is a common enough thing.
explanation.walkthrough: VALE is the Latin farewell; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Prevalent means widespread or common, the opposite of rare.

clue.text: Regularly walk and run — it shows odd behaviour

parts.note: to march is to walk with a regular step
to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: Walking at a steady pace and then running is a sign of eccentricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad as a March hare' is a proverb; Carroll's character is the Hatter's companion at the tea party.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially mad, this creature behaves strangely in the breeding season.

clue.text: Girl not reflecting and plunging into adventures

definitions.text: Girl not reflecting and plunging into adventures

parts.words: Girl not reflecting and plunging into adventures
parts.note: a heedless girl, but also the heroine who tumbles down a rabbit hole in the first book rather than stepping through a mirror in the second

explanation.surface: A thoughtless girl dives headlong into escapades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not reflecting' looks like thoughtlessness but means not in the Looking-glass book.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's heroine falls down the rabbit hole at the start of her adventures.

clue.text: Repeatedly act as race organiser

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word for act appears twice

parts.note: to do is to act

explanation.surface: Acting again and again as the person running a race.
explanation.walkthrough: In Wonderland the extinct bird organises the Caucus-race, in which everyone wins.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's dodo sets up the Caucus-race to dry everyone off.

clue.text: Country looking fantastic visited after fall

definitions.text: Country looking fantastic visited after fall

parts.words: Country looking fantastic visited after fall
parts.note: read as a lovely land toured in autumn, but it is the dream realm reached by tumbling down a rabbit hole

explanation.surface: A beautiful landscape seen on an autumn holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' suggests autumn, as Americans say, but is Alice's drop down the rabbit hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The marvellous dream realm of Carroll's first book is reached after a long drop.
